steps.title: Validate input data formats
steps.instruction: Ensure all input files follow the specifications in the README.md and contain a header row (header = TRUE). Verify that the R data frames exist and have the required columns: gffs (Gene, chr, start, end, …), exp_m (genes as rows, individuals as columns, log2‑transformed and quantile‑normalized TPMs), genes (character vector of target gene IDs), K (kinship matrix), and pheno (phenotypic data with individual IDs as row names). Prepare the files listed in Table 2 with the exact names and types:

substeps.instruction: --gffs_file: RData file gffs.RData containing gene annotation.
--exp_file: RData file exp_matrix.RData containing the normalized expression matrix.
--genodir: Pathname to the directory with PLINK binary genotype files (.bed, .bim, .fam) organized per chromosome.
--gfile_prefix: String pattern for genotype file names, e.g. "%s_529_test" where %s is the chromosome number.
--K_file: RData file Kinship.RData containing the kinship matrix.
--pheno_file: RData file pheno.RData containing phenotypic data.
--gene_file: RData file genes.RData containing the vector of target gene IDs.

steps.title: Interpret cistrans‑twas results
steps.instruction: For each trait, a .csv file is generated. Genes are ranked by the rank_product, defined as the geometric mean of the p‑value ranks from the cis‑EC and trans‑EC associations; a smaller rank_product indicates a higher likelihood of causality.

steps.title: Interpret cistrans‑etwas results
steps.instruction: For each target gene listed in gene_file, a .csv result file is produced. Genes are ranked by rank_product; top‑ranked genes are candidate upstream regulators of the target gene. The output includes columns such as chr, start, end, strand, beta_cis, se_cis, zscore_cis, q‑value_cis, beta_trans, se_trans, zscore_trans, q‑value_trans, cis_rank, trans_rank, and Qsymbols.
